title: Tool runner: deterministic chaining, idempotent result injection, and recursion guards
creator: Anika Rao
description: Objective: implement a robust tool execution loop that supports deterministic multi-tool chaining, safe and idempotent injection of tool results into model context, and reliable recursion/loop guards. Scope: core runtime + API surface + SDK compatibility shim. Non-goals: changing tool auth model, adding new types of tools beyond current observation/response model.
background: We currently allow single tool calls and ad hoc result injection for orchestration flows. Increasingly customers and internal features require chained tool sequences (e.g., search -> fetch -> summarize -> cite) with streaming and structured outputs. Missing primitives: a deterministic execution ordering, a standard marker for injected results, and robust loop detection to prevent runaway or adversarial tool cycles.
proposed_design:
1) Execution DAG + deterministic ordering: represent requested tool calls as a linearized DAG using explicit call IDs and numeric ordering to ensure reproducible run order across retries and between SDKs.
2) Result injection protocol: tool results are injected as 'observations' with a signed metadata header (runner_signature:v1, call_id, tool_version, content_type) so the model and downstream tooling can distinguish injected content from user input. Injections are idempotent — each call_id can only be injected once per request context.
3) Recursion/loop guards: three-tier protection: max_depth (configurable, default 6), cycle-detection via stable hash of (call_id, tool_name, canonicalized_input) plus recent history TTL, and budget guard that tracks cumulative tool CPU/IO time and aborts with a structured error if budget exceeded.
4) Streaming compatibility: tool outputs can stream partial observations; the runner buffers streaming chunks and injects checkpointed structured fragments with incremental signatures so the model can consume partial structured outputs while respecting idempotency.
5) Backwards compatibility layer: SDK shim detects older client behavior and maps legacy injection patterns to the new protocol using a compatibility header; the control plane exposes a feature flag to gate behavior per-tenant.
tradeoffs_and_risks:
- Deterministic ordering simplifies retry semantics but constrains some opportunistic parallelism.
- Signing/metadata increases payload size; we must measure token overhead vs safety benefits.
- Conservative default max_depth may break some existing long workflows; will offer opt-out but lock behind admin controls.
- Cycle detection false positives if canonicalization rules are too aggressive; we will iterate on normalization rules.
acceptance_criteria: Deterministic call ordering implemented and covered by unit tests for retries and partial failures.
Injected observations include runner_signature and obey idempotency (duplicate injection attempts ignored and logged).
Loop guards trigger and return structured error code TOOL_LOOP_DETECTED in integration tests that simulate cycles.
Streaming tool outputs can be consumed by the model in incremental mode without duplicating injected content.
Compatibility shim supports v1 and legacy SDKs and is feature-flagged per-tenant.
Monitoring dashboard shows tool call counts, average depth, loop abort rate, and errors; thresholds defined for rollout gating.
implementation_notes: Runtime: add call_id and ordering fields to ToolCall protobuf and persist in request context.
Injection: produce signed-metadata header using control-plane keypair; public key available to model evaluation hooks.
Loop detection: store LRU of recent canonical hashes in request state; TTL 10 minutes by default.
Budgeting: integrate with existing per-request budget meter (tokens + runtime_ms). Abort path returns structured JSON error with retryable=false.
SDKs: add compatibility shim in JS and Python that rewrites legacy 'inject' calls to new runner signature.
Telemetry: emit events tool.exec.start, tool.exec.end, tool.inject.*, tool.loop.detected with tags: tenant, model, call_count.
rollout_plan: Feature-flag behind control-plane toggle 'tool_runner_v2' default off.
Alpha rollout to internal teams (console, solutions) for 1 week with enhanced logging.
Canary to 5% of prod tenants for 2 weeks; require loop abort rate < 0.05% and no user-visible failures in the canary cohort.
Gradual ramp to 50% then 100% with 24h observation windows and automated rollback on SLO regressions.
Communication: SDK release notes, migration guide, and design doc link on Confluence.
test_plan: Unit tests for idempotent injection and duplicate suppression.
Integration tests: simulated chain (search->fetch->summarize->cite) including streaming variants.
Fuzz tests: adversarial prompts designed to trigger recursion and malformed tool outputs.
Load tests: measure overhead of signed metadata at 10k TPS-equivalent to quantify token and latency impact.
Security review: validate signature scheme and ensure no private keys leak to tenant code.
